ip_top_stories.title: Universal and Sony Want Suno's Newest AI Models Exposed in 60K-Recording Copyright Battle
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to compel Suno to disclose its newest AI models as part of the ongoing copyright litigation involving approximately 60,000 recordings. The labels are pushing to expand the scope of discovery to include Suno's latest model releases. The case is a major test of AI training liability in the music industry.

ip_top_stories.title: Reservoir Widens AI Copyright Suits Against Suno and Anthropic to Over 2,500 Songs
ip_top_stories.summary: Music publisher Reservoir has expanded its AI copyright lawsuits against both Suno and Anthropic, now covering more than 2,500 songs. The move signals escalating legal pressure on AI developers from the music publishing sector. The suits allege unauthorised use of copyrighted musical works in AI training.

ip_top_stories.title: Elvis rights holders and Eminem's publisher sue Suno, testing the ELVIS Act
ip_top_stories.summary: Rights holders for Elvis Presley and Eminem's music publisher have filed suit against AI music platform Suno, invoking Tennessee's ELVIS Act in what is considered a significant test of the new law protecting artists' voices and likenesses. The case extends the legal front against Suno beyond traditional copyright claims. It raises questions about the intersection of personality rights legislation and AI-generated music.

ip_top_stories.title: Court allows news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to go ahead
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has permitted a copyright lawsuit brought by news publishers against OpenAI to proceed, marking a significant development in the ongoing legal battles over AI training on journalistic content. The ruling allows publishers to pursue claims that OpenAI used their articles without authorisation. The decision adds to growing judicial scrutiny of AI companies' data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: The Anatomy of
: An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen interviews IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on how the global reproduction rights community is framing the question of harm in the context of AI and copyright. Huss-Ekerhult outlines the challenges rights organisations face in asserting collective licensing frameworks against AI developers. The piece provides substantive policy context for the broader debate over AI training and rights holder compensation.

ip_further_links.title: AI firms trying to turn Australia into copyright 'tax haven': Rod Sims
ip_further_links.summary: Former ACCC chair Rod Sims accuses AI companies of attempting to exploit Australia's opt-out copyright framework, describing efforts to avoid paying rights holders as an attempt to create a copyright tax haven.

ip_further_links.title: 'Deeply flawed': Former ACCC boss slams opt-out AI copyright plan
ip_further_links.summary: Rod Sims criticises Australia's proposed opt-out model for AI copyright as deeply flawed, arguing it unfairly burdens rights holders who should not have to actively protect their own works from AI ingestion.

ip_further_links.title: Google, Meta, TikTok Oppose Indonesia's AI Copyright Bill
ip_further_links.summary: Major US tech platforms are lobbying against Indonesia's proposed AI copyright legislation, which would require AI companies to compensate rights holders for use of their content in training data.

ip_further_links.title: 'Not simply a UK copyright issue': A US perspective on Getty v Stability AI
ip_further_links.summary: Legal analysis offers a US-focused view on the Getty Images v Stability AI case, arguing the litigation has significant implications beyond UK copyright law for how AI image generation and training are regulated globally.

ip_further_links.title: Friends of the Court Flock to the OpenAI Copyright Fight
ip_further_links.summary: Multiple amicus briefs are being filed in the OpenAI copyright litigation as a broad range of stakeholders seek to influence how courts interpret AI training and fair use.

ip_further_links.title: In landmark AI copyright settlement, this Keene author's getting a cut
ip_further_links.summary: A New Hampshire author is set to receive compensation as part of a landmark AI copyright settlement, illustrating how individual authors may benefit from class-action legal action against AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic, OpenAI sued for allegedly infringing inventors' neural network patents
ip_further_links.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI face a new lawsuit alleging their AI systems infringe patents relating to neural network inventions, adding a patent dimension to the mounting IP litigation against leading AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Publishers face Google AI ad labels in California, South Korea and Vietnam
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers in multiple jurisdictions are encountering Google's AI-generated ad labels, raising concerns about the impact on content visibility and revenue for news and publishing organisations.

ip_further_links.title: 6th Annual Symposium on Pop Culture and International Law: Ownership of a Style - Ghibli-Style Generation and the Limits of Copyright within the Territorial Framework
ip_further_links.summary: An academic symposium examines the copyright implications of AI-generated Ghibli-style imagery, exploring the limits of style protection and the territorial nature of copyright law across jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Disney Moves Beyond AI Copyright Battles to Develop Its Own AI Tools
ip_further_links.summary: Disney is reported to be developing proprietary AI tools even as it remains involved in AI copyright disputes, signalling a dual-track approach of litigation and internal AI adoption.
